data.title: Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of The Chemours Company Class Action Lawsuit
data.description:
Investor Alert: Robbins LLP Informs Investors of The Chemours Company Class Action Lawsuit

Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP informs investors that a class action was filed on behalf of persons or entities who purchased or otherwise acquired The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC) securities between February 20, 2026 and August 4, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). Chemours offers a range of industrial and specialty chemical products for markets including, refrigeration and air conditioning.

The complaint alleges that Chemours materially overstated market demand for its products.

Investors who purchased Chemours securities during the Class Period and suffered significant losses should contact Robbins LLP for information about the lawsuit and the December 7, 2026 lead plaintiff motion deadline.

Why Was Chemours Sued?

The complaint alleges that, during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose that:

  1. defendants had materially overstated aftermarket demand for their Opteon products;
  2. demand for such products was decreasing because of defendants’ overselling Opteon products in the preceding fiscal year;
  3. as a result of these undisclosed issues, defendants’ financial guidance for the 2026 fiscal year was unreliable; and
  4. as a result, defendants’ public statements were materially false and misleading at all relevant times.

Why Did Chemours Stock Drop?

Plaintiff alleges that on August 4, 2026, after market hours, Chemours announced second quarter 2026 financial results. Among other things, the Company reduced its adjusted EBITDA full-year guidance to $775 million to $825 million (from $800 million to $900 million previously). Further, on the accompanying earnings call, management admitted that “[a]s a result of the initial channel fill, aftermarket customers built additional inventory, creating an oversupplied channel heading into 2026.” Management further disclosed “from the Q2 and Q3 perspective, there’s probably about $65 million of aftermarket sales that realistically, you think about like-for-like probably should have been allocated to more of this year.” On this news, Chemours’s stock price fell $3.34 per share, or 18.63%, to close at $14.59 per share on August 5, 2026.

What Can Chemours Shareholders Do Now?

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired The Chemours Company securities during the Class Period may be eligible to serve as lead plaintiff. The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Stockholders who wish to seek appointment as lead plaintiff must move the court no later than December 7, 2026. Contact Robbins LLP for information about the appointment process.

Shareholders do not need to serve as lead plaintiff to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis, with no upfront or out-of-pocket fees or expenses.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about The Chemours Company securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history.

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against The Chemours Company settles, or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

Arcus Biosciences Announces New Employment Inducement Grants

Arcus Biosciences, Inc. (NYSE:RCUS), a clinical-stage, global biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated molecules and combination therapies for the treatment of cancer and inflammatory diseases, today announced that the Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors granted 2 new employees options to purchase a total of 9,150 shares of the Company’s common stock at an exercise price per share of $23.83, which was the closing price on October 8, 2026, and restricted stock units to acquire a total of 4,600 shares of the Company’s common stock. The equity awards were granted pursuant to the Company’s 2020 Inducement Plan, which was approved by the Company’s Board of Directors in January 2020 pursuant to the “inducement exception” under NYSE Listed Company Manual Rule 303A.08.

About Arcus Biosciences

Arcus Biosciences is a clinical-stage, global biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated molecules for the treatment of cancer and inflammatory diseases. In partnership with industry collaborators, patients and physicians around the world, Arcus is expediting the development of its late-stage portfolio of first- and/or best-in-class medicines against well-characterized biological targets and pathways and studying novel, biology-driven combinations that have the potential to help people with cancer live longer. Founded in 2015, the company has advanced multiple investigational medicines into registrational clinical trials including casdatifan, a HIF-2α inhibitor for clear cell renal cell carcinoma, and quemliclustat, a small-molecule CD73 inhibitor for pancreatic cancer. For more information about Arcus Biosciences’ clinical and preclinical programs, please visit www.arcusbio.com.

data.title: Accendra Health Receives Continued Listing Standard Notice from NYSE; Intends to Cure Deficiency and Return to Compliance with NYSE Listing Standard
data.description:
Accendra Health Receives Continued Listing Standard Notice from NYSE; Intends to Cure Deficiency and Return to Compliance with NYSE Listing Standard

 

Accendra Health, Inc. (NYSE: ACH) (the Company) today announced that on October 6, 2026, it received a notice (the “Notice”) from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) notifying the Company that it is not in compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing standards because the average closing price of the Company’s Class A Common Stock (the “Common Stock”) was less than $1.00 per share over a consecutive 30 trading-day period. The Notice does not result in the immediate delisting of the Company’s Common Stock from the NYSE.

The Company intends to respond to the NYSE within ten business days of receipt of the Notice affirming its intent to cure the deficiency. Pursuant to the NYSE’s rules, the Company has a six-month period following receipt of the Notice to regain compliance with the NYSE’s minimum share price requirement.

The Company intends to consider a number of available alternatives to cure its non-compliance with the applicable price criteria in the NYSE’s continued listing standards including, if necessary, a reverse stock split that would be subject to stockholder approval no later than at the Company’s next annual meeting of stockholders anticipated to take place in May 2027. The Company can regain compliance with the minimum share price requirement at any time during the six-month cure period if, on the last trading day of any calendar month during the cure period or on the last day of the cure period, the Company has (i) a closing share price of at least $1.00, and (ii) an average closing share price of at least $1.00 over the 30 trading-day periods ending on the last trading day of that month.

The Company’s Common Stock will continue to be listed and trade on the NYSE during this period, subject to its compliance with other NYSE continued listing standards. The receipt of the Notice does not affect the Company’s business, operations or reporting requirements with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Country music star Zach Bryan buys $18 million, 40-acre Tennessee estate after getting married
data.description:
By Kelsi Karruli

Bryan reportedly bought the property earlier this year; it has a huge barn with a recording studio.

Zach Bryan performs September 2026.

Country star Zach Bryan has reportedly forked over $18.25 million for a sprawling estate in Franklin, Tenn.-months after tying the knot with Samantha Leonard.

Bryan, 30-who said "I do" in late 2025 following his highly publicized and tumultuous romance with influencer Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia-picked up the palatial property earlier this year, according to TMZ.

Reportedly set on 40 acres, the estate offers plenty of privacy for the musician and his new wife, along with an impressive space for Bryan to work on his music in the comfort of his home.

Zach Bryan and Brianna LaPaglia in 2024 in Los Angeles.

The main residence spans 5,035 square feet and features four bedrooms and five bathrooms, along with a wraparound porch with unencumbered views of the surrounding Tennessee hills.

The expansive grounds are outfitted with two ponds, lush gardens, and walking trails, as well as a resort-style swimming pool and an outdoor kitchen.

However, one of the property's most impressive features is an enormous 5,300-square-foot barn.

Far from a traditional agricultural structure, the barn has been transformed into an entertainment and creative hub, complete with a grand bar, video wall, fireplaces, a game room, gym, and catering kitchen.

There are also two bedroom suites and a two-car garage.

Perhaps most fittingly for its Grammy-winning new owner, the barn boasts a massive recording studio, allowing Bryan to work on new music just steps from his home.

News of the singer's splashy purchase comes months after he and Leonard got married in Spain in late 2025.

The pair were first romantically linked in summer 2025. Their marriage marked a new chapter for Bryan after his messy and very public breakup with LaPaglia, who previously claimed that she had been offered millions of dollars-and, at one point, Bryan's Massachusetts home-in exchange for remaining silent about their relationship.

In July 2025, the former couple's breakup once again spilled into the public eye when Bryan shared screenshots of messages he claimed LaPaglia had sent after their romance ended.

One screenshot appeared to show a lengthy message from LaPaglia reflecting on her feelings about their 2024 split. In it, she said she would "never forget the love" she once felt for Bryan and insisted that she had never been interested in his "lifestyle or money."

She also wrote that she believed she "deserved a goodbye" and asked Bryan to take care of their shared cat, Stump, and give his dog, Jack, a hug on her behalf.

More from Realtor.com: Squatters Take Over $4.4 Million San Francisco Mansion With Bizarre Ownership History

Bryan also posted a screenshot of another message that appeared to have been sent by LaPaglia to a third party and outlined several alleged "options" available to her in the aftermath of the breakup.

One purported option involved taking a $12 million payment to stay publicly silent about the split. Another was accepting Bryan's Duxbury home in exchange for dropping allegations about their relationship. The final option was a "messy war," where LaPaglia would go public with her experiences.

Bryan quickly deleted the screenshots, but LaPaglia responded with several posts of her own, including what she claimed was a message from Bryan's manager detailing potential terms of an NDA.

According to the screenshot she shared, one proposed deal involved Bryan's "Duxbury house + 3 million," while another involved a $10 million cash payment.

More from Realtor.com: How I used a VA Assumable Loan to Buy a 3-Bedroom Home in San Antonio-and My Monthly Mortgage is $980

LaPaglia later insisted that she had "not told one lie ever" about her relationship with Bryan and claimed that she had ultimately turned down an offer worth $12.9 million.

At the time of their breakup, LaPaglia had been living in Bryan's $7.45 million Massachusetts mansion, which the singer purchased in April 2024.

By November of that year, a moving truck had been spotted outside the property, and LaPaglia later revealed that she had moved out and was searching for a place of her own in New York City-a process she documented on TikTok.

More from Realtor.com: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear Says Next President Must Make 'Bold Investment' in Housing

The Duxbury Bay mansion is believed to be the property referenced in one of the alleged post-breakup offers.

The waterfront residence boasts sweeping views of the bay, along with a private boathouse and pier.

Inside, it has five bedrooms and 6.5 bathrooms, as well as an expanded living space with a fireplace and a spacious kitchen.

Before Bryan purchased the property, it had spent nearly a year on the market and was listed for $8.9 million in August 2023.

More from Realtor.com: The Hidden Gem Short-Term Rental Markets of 2026: Where Owners Are Maximizing Returns

Bryan owns another property nearby, according to records, which show that a second Duxbury home was purchased for $1.4 million in August 2024 through the same LLC used for the waterfront estate. Bryan is listed as a manager of the LLC.

That residence sits closer to the center of town, roughly a four-minute drive from the Duxbury Bay mansion. Built in 1910, the property features three bedrooms and 2.5 bathrooms.

data.title: Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation
data.description:
Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation

Packaging Expert Kyle Reger Explains Cost-Effective Packaging Beyond Box Prices in HelloNation

PR Newswire

ROCHESTER, N.Y., Oct. 9, 2026

The Article Examines How Packaging Choices Affect Shipping Costs, Product Protection, Labor Efficiency, Storage, and Long-Term Operating Expenses.

ROCHESTER, N.Y., Oct. 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- What makes packaging truly cost-effective? HelloNation answers that question inan article featuring insights from Packaging Expert Kyle Reger, Regional Sales Manager at Jamestown Container Companies in Rochester, New York.

The article explains that evaluating cost-effective packaging requires looking beyond the price of an individual box. While procurement teams often start with the purchase price, the article notes that packaging decisions affect nearly every step of the supply chain. Shipping efficiency, product protection, labor requirements, storage needs, and overall operational performance all contribute to the total cost of ownership.

According to the HelloNation article, one of the most significant factors influencing packaging costs is product protection. Packaging that fits products properly helps reduce damage during transportation and handling. Fewer damaged shipments can lower replacement expenses, reduce return shipping, minimize customer service issues, and prevent production delays. The article explains that even modest improvements in damage rates can create substantial savings when spread across large shipping volumes.

The article also describes how packaging design directly influences shipping costs. Oversized boxes often increase dimensional freight charges while requiring additional filler materials. Right-sized packaging improves freight efficiency by maximizing trailer space, increasing pallet utilization, and moving more products in fewer shipments. These improvements help organizations control transportation expenses while maintaining reliable product protection throughout delivery.

The HelloNation article emphasizes that packaging evaluations should carefully consider labor costs. Packaging that assembles quickly or simplifies packing lets employees work more efficiently. Small improvements in box design or packing methods can reduce repetitive tasks and speed up production. Over thousands of shipments, saving only a few seconds per package may translate into meaningful labor savings for many organizations.

Storage efficiency is another area where packaging choices influence long-term value. The article explains that packaging designed to nest efficiently or ship flat can reduce the amount of storage space required for inventory. Better organization also makes packaging materials easier to access during daily operations, helping warehouse teams work more efficiently while reducing unnecessary handling.

Throughout the article, Packaging Expert Kyle Reger explains that procurement decisions should consider the full operational impact of packaging, not just the initial purchase price. The article encourages procurement teams to compare product damage rates, freight expenses, labor efficiency, storage capacity, packaging consistency, and compatibility with existing workflows. Considering all these factors together provides a clearer picture of total packaging costs.

The article further notes that successful packaging decisions come from understanding how every stage of the supply chain connects to the next. Poorly fitting packaging may create unnecessary waste, require excess packing materials, slow production, increase freight expenses, or contribute to avoidable product damage. By considering the broader operational picture, organizations can identify cost-effective packaging solutions that improve efficiency while supporting dependable day-to-day operations.

What Makes Packaging Cost-Effective Beyond the Box Price features insights from Kyle Reger, a packaging expert in Rochester, New York, on HelloNation.

Jamestown Container Companies is a family-owned packaging manufacturer headquartered in Falconer, New York. Since 1956, the company has provided custom corrugated packaging, packaging supplies, displays, and contract packaging services to customers throughout the Great Lakes region. Jamestown Container Companies operates multiple facilities across New York and Ohio and is committed to delivering innovative, cost-effective, and environmentally responsible packaging solutions.
